RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 25

An all-male panel is not evidence of bias by itself. In senior ministry recruitment it's statistically common, and panels of four men appointing a man happen constantly without discrimination. Treating it as your main argument would be easy to dismiss and would weaken the stronger point.

Your stronger point is procedural: your qualifications look at least equal on paper, and they've ignored a two-week-old request for written reasons — which in most jurisdictions you're entitled to.

So: chase the written explanation formally, in writing, with a deadline. Ask for the scoring criteria and how each candidate scored. Mention panel composition only as one factual detail if the reasons turn out to be vague, inconsistent, or criteria that appeared after the fact.
